paper.title: Cross-scale covariance for material property prediction
paper.research_summary: The paper proposes a statistical approach to predict large-scale material properties (specifically plastic flow strength in FCC metals) using regression on small-scale 'indicator' properties computed with the same interatomic potential (IP). It analyzes covariance between MD-simulated flow strength (QoI) and 39 small-scale properties (e.g., elastic constants, surface energies, vacancy migration energy) across a pool of 153 IPs from OpenKIM. A multi-linear regression model is built and validated to predict flow strength from small-scale predictors, with error bounds estimated via cross-validation. The model is then applied to DFT-computed predictors to estimate flow strength for seven FCC metals.

tasks.task_name_raw: predicting plastic flow strength from small-scale indicator properties
tasks.objective: To predict large-scale plastic flow strength of FCC metals using statistical regression on computationally cheaper small-scale indicator properties that are covariant with the target property.
constraints: Predictors must be computable at small scales (≤10² atoms) where FP calculations are feasible
Regression model must generalize to first-principles (DFT) predictor values
input_requirements: Small-scale indicator properties computed with the same interatomic potential
output_goal: Predicted plastic flow strength value with quantified uncertainty bounds

evidence.text: Here we explore covariance between predictions of metal plasticity, from 178 large-scale (~108 atoms) molecular dynamics (MD) simulations, and a variety of indicator properties computed at small-scales (≤102 atoms). All simulations use the same 178 IPs. In a manner similar to statistical studies in public health, we analyze correlations of strength with indicators, identify the best predictor properties, and build a cross-scale “strength-on-predictors” regression model.

As a test bed in the material simulation context, we examine the covariance of dislocation-based plastic flow strength in face-centered cubic (FCC) metals (our QoI) computed in large-scale molecular dynamics (MD) simulations with indicator properties of the same materials computable on small scales, e.g., elastic constants, surface energies, etc.

stages.stage_name_raw: collecting interatomic potential models and their precomputed properties
stages.stage_goal: Acquire a statistically representative pool of interatomic potentials and their associated small-scale property predictions.
stage_output: Precomputed small-scale indicator properties from OpenKIM

evidence.text: Out of the many IPs available and documented in the OpenKIM repository, 178 IPs previously developed for nine FCC metals were selected.
The IPs used are available in the OpenKIM repository at https://openkim.org4 along with their predictions for a range of material properties computed using robust and vetted computational protocols.

stages.stage_name_raw: screening IP models for numerical and physical validity
stages.stage_goal: Remove IP models exhibiting numerical instabilities or physically anomalous behavior during MD simulations.
stage_output: 163 IPs after removing 15 due to instabilities or anomalies

evidence.text: MD simulations using one particular IP could not be completed due to numerical instabilities encountered irrespective of the integration time step. Another 14 IPs were excluded after subsequent analyzes revealed anomalies or irregularities in crystal response to straining, such as crystal rotation, phase transformations, and formation of amorphous phases, or voids (see the Supplementary Information (SI) for the full list of IPs and details on which were removed from consideration).

stages.stage_name_raw: cleaning and imputing missing or unreliable small-scale property data
stages.stage_goal: Ensure completeness and reliability of the small-scale indicator property dataset for regression modeling.

evidence.text: At the same time, inspection of small-scale indicator properties of the remaining 163 IPs, precomputed in the OpenKIM repository, revealed some missing or out-of-bounds values deemed unreliable. Out of 62 initially considered indicators, 27 properties contained numerous missing or unreliable values and were excluded from our study altogether. To fill the gaps in the 163 × 35 table of the remaining small-scale properties, wherever possible we (1) computed the missing property values, and (2) re-computed property values falling outside of their physically reasonable range. Still, some properties for several IPs could not be re-computed or remained unreasonable: all such IP samples were excluded from computing covariance of strength with their missing small-scale properties (see SI for details).

Here we use data imputation to replace missing and unreasonable indicator values with inferred values, based on a k-nearest neighbors approach (see SI for details). We again relied on expert opinion to bound ranges of reasonable values for small-scale property data; however, all decisions as to which property values to exclude or replace were made prior to statistical analysis.

stages.stage_name_raw: identifying and excluding SF-jammed IP models
stages.stage_goal: Remove IP models exhibiting qualitatively different plastic response (stacking fault jamming) to ensure statistical homogeneity.

evidence.text: Of the 16 models that were identified as SF jammed, six had been previously excluded from the statistical pool based on other considerations. Outliers or not, we excluded all SF jammed IPs from further statistical analyses on the grounds that they exhibit a plastic response qualitatively different from the rest of the remaining IP models, thus paring our statistical pool down to 153 IP models (see SI for details).

stages.stage_goal: Generate additional candidate small-scale indicator properties motivated by physical insights into dislocation-vacancy interactions.
stage_input: Observations of vacancy clusters in MD simulations
Physical hypothesis about vacancy production increasing resistance
stage_output: Four new vacancy-related indicators: relaxed/unrelaxed vacancy formation energy, vacancy migration barrier, vacancy formation volume

evidence.text: Following this logic, we developed new Open-KIM property calculations (KIM test drivers) for computing the vacancy formation energy (both relaxed and unrelaxed), the vacancy migration barrier, and the vacancy formation volume10,11.

stages.stage_name_raw: training multi-linear regression models on indicator properties
stages.stage_goal: Build statistical regression models relating plastic flow strength to combinations of small-scale indicator properties.
stage_input: 153 IPs with complete small-scale property data

evidence.text: We use multi-linear regression to illustrate the construction of a statistical model relating ﬂow strength to the indicator properties, leaving more advanced regression analyses to the SI. Prior to computing regression coefﬁcients each variable in the regression model is shifted and scaled to have zero mean and unit variance6.

stages.stage_name_raw: evaluating regression model performance with cross-validation
stages.stage_goal: Quantify goodness-of-fit and prediction error of the regression models using statistical cross-validation.

evidence.text: Figure 2d is the plot of the standard goodness of ﬁt parameter r 2 as a function of the number of predictors included in the multi-linear regression, in descending order of their correlation with strength. Although r2 rises monotonically with the number of included predictors (as it should), except for several notable increases, adding more predictors brings little improvement in the goodness of ﬁt.

Here, we ﬁt 153 regression models on the same three predictors, leaving out one of the 153 IP samples from each model for validation. As an estimate of the prediction error by regression on DFT predictors, the average relative prediction error among 153 leave-one-out models is 15%.
evidence.section: Predicting ﬂow strength by regression on ﬁrst-principles data

stages.stage_name_raw: validating regression predictions against DFT-computed predictors
stages.stage_goal: Apply the trained regression model to first-principles (DFT) computed small-scale predictors to estimate plastic flow strength and assess predictive capability.
stage_input: DFT-computed {111} surface energy, lattice constant, and vacancy migration energy for seven FCC metals
stage_output: Predicted plastic flow strength values for Ag, Al, Au, Cu, Ni, Pd, Pt

evidence.text: We used FP DFT calculations to compute the predictor properties used in the 3-variable regression model shown in Fig. 4b, i.e., the {111} surface energy, the lattice constant, and the VME. Figure 5 shows the ﬂow strength of seven FCC metals Ag, Al, Au, Cu, Ni, Pd, and Pt, predicted by substituting into the regression model the three predictors computed for each metal using DFT (see the “Methods” section for the details of the DFT calculations and the SI for a table of DFT results). Assuming that the 153 IPs and the seven DFT models belong to the same statistical pool (see explanation above), these values represent what seven hypothetical MD simulations with DFT forces would have predicted if indeed they could be performed under the same simulation conditions as those performed with the IPs.
evidence.section: Predicting ﬂow strength by regression on ﬁrst-principles data

evidence.text: The IPs used are available in the OpenKIM repository at https://openkim.org4 along with their predictions for a range of material properties computed using robust and vetted computational protocols.
OpenKIM4,17 (Open Knowledgebase of Interatomic Models) is a multi-faceted cyberinfrastructure project founded in 2009. All content on OpenKIM is publicly available at https://openkim.org.
Out of the many IPs available and documented in the OpenKIM repository, 178 IPs previously developed for nine FCC metals were selected.

Here we explore covariance between predictions of metal plasticity, from 178 large-scale (~108 atoms) molecular dynamics (MD) simulations, and a variety of indicator properties computed at small-scales (≤102 atoms). All simulations use the same 178 IPs.

MD simulations using one particular IP could not be completed due to numerical instabilities encountered irrespective of the integration time step. Another 14 IPs were excluded after subsequent analyzes revealed anomalies or irregularities in crystal response to straining, such as crystal rotation, phase transformations, and formation of amorphous phases, or voids (see the Supplementary Information (SI) for the full list of IPs and details on which were removed from consideration).
At the same time, inspection of small-scale indicator properties of the remaining 163 IPs, precomputed in the OpenKIM repository, revealed some missing or out-of-bounds values deemed unreliable.
